_comment: Grade 1 is for ages 6-7, who cannot read yet: every teaching lesson reads its prompt aloud on opening (internal/readsAloud.ts), and the speaker button reads each question, each answer and the reason after an answer, one line at a time so each line matches its own clip.

Generated: run `node scripts/science-voice-lines.mjs` after changing any words in locales/en.json or lessons.json; science.test.ts fails if this file is out of date. Record with `npm run voice:science` (OpenAI). Khmer lines use live speech.
prompts: Is it living or not living? Tap the group it belongs to.
What do living things need? Tap the answer.
Which part of your body helps you? Tap it.
Which part of the plant does this job? Tap it.
What helps this animal? Tap the answer.
What does this baby grow into? Tap the answer.
How does the parent help? Tap the answer.
How does it grow? Put the pictures in order.
What happens to the sound? Tap the answer.
What does light do? Tap the answer.
Does it make its own light? Tap the group.
Does light go through it? Tap the group.
What happens in the sky? Tap the answer.
What comes first? Put the pictures in order.
What is the weather like? Tap the answer.
phrases: Have another look, then try again.
The leaves are dry and drooping. What does this plant need?
Water
Darkness
A blanket
Plants need water. The roots drink it up from the soil.
Plants need light, not darkness, to grow.
What do plants need to make their own food?
Sunlight
Rice
Milk
Green leaves use sunlight to make food for the plant.
Plants do not eat food like we do. They make their own.
Plants do not drink milk. They make their own food.
A fish lives in water. Does a fish need air?
Yes, it gets air from the water
No, fish never need air
Yes. A fish breathes with its gills. Gills take in the air that is mixed into the water.
All animals need air. A fish gets its air from the water.
Which one does NOT need food?
Cat
Hen
Child
Toy robot
A toy robot is not alive. Living things need food. Toys do not.
A cat is alive, so it needs food.
A hen is alive, so it needs food.
You are alive, so you need food!
Why do farmers keep water in rice fields?
Rice plants need water to grow
Water makes rice white
Water keeps the Sun away
Rice plants need lots of water to grow. They grow well in wet fields.
Water does not change the colour of rice. The plants need it to grow.
What does a puppy need to grow?
Food, water and air
Only sunlight
Only toys
Animals need food, water and air to live and grow.
Plants make food from sunlight. Animals must eat food.
The rooster crows. Which part helps you hear it?
Ear
Eye
Nose
We hear sounds with our ears.
You smell a durian. Which part helps you smell?
Hand
We smell with our nose.
A green mango tastes sour. Which part tastes it?
Tongue
We taste with our tongue: sweet, sour, salty and bitter.
You see a rainbow. Which part helps you see?
We see with our eyes.
Ice feels cold. Which part feels it?
Skin on your hand
Our skin feels hot and cold, soft and rough.
Is it safe to look straight at the Sun?
No, it can hurt your eyes
Yes, for a long time
No. The Sun is so bright it can hurt your eyes. Never look straight at it.
Looking at the Sun can hurt your eyes, even for a short time.
You smell smoke at home. What should you do?
Tell a grown-up at once
Go back to sleep
Tell a grown-up at once. Your nose can warn you of danger.
Smoke can mean a fire. Always tell a grown-up straight away.
Which part takes in water from the soil?
Roots
Leaves
Flower
Roots grow down into the soil and soak up water.
Leaves are up in the light. The water is in the soil.
Which part holds the plant up straight?
Stem
Leaf
The stem holds the plant up and carries water to the leaves.
Which part uses sunlight to make food?
Seed
Green leaves use sunlight, air and water to make food for the plant.
Roots are in the dark soil. Making food needs sunlight.
Which part can grow into a fruit?
A flower can grow into a fruit with seeds inside.
Which part of a mango can grow into a new mango tree?
The seed can grow into a new plant.
A lotus grows in a pond. Which part is down in the mud?
Lotus roots grow in the mud. The leaves and flower reach up to the light.
What helps a fish swim?
Fins and tail
Gills
Scales
A fish swims by moving its fins and tail.
Gills help a fish breathe, not swim.
Scales cover the fish and keep it safe.
What helps a bird fly?
Wings
Beak
Feet
Birds flap their wings to fly.
A beak helps a bird eat. It does not help it fly.
What keeps a turtle safe from danger?
Its hard shell
Its tail
Its eyes
A turtle pulls its head and legs into its hard shell.
Why can a duck swim so well?
Webbed feet push the water
It has a flat beak
It has two eyes
Skin between a duck's toes pushes the water, like a paddle.
What does an elephant use to pick up food and drink water?
Trunk
Ears
Tail
An elephant's trunk is its long nose. It grabs food and sucks up water.
Why does a rabbit have big ears?
To hear danger far away
To fly
To swim
Big ears catch quiet sounds, so a rabbit can hear danger and run away.
This baby is a tadpole. What does it grow into?
Frog
Fish
Bird
A tadpole grows legs, loses its tail and becomes a frog.
A tadpole swims like a fish, but it grows legs and becomes a frog.
This baby is a chick. What does it grow into?
Duck
A chick grows into a hen or a rooster, like its parents.
A baby duck is a duckling. A chick grows into a hen or a rooster.
This baby is a caterpillar. What does it grow into?
Butterfly
Snail
A caterpillar makes a case called a chrysalis, then comes out as a butterfly.
Kittens and their mother. How do they look?
Alike, but not exactly the same
Exactly the same
Not alike at all
Babies look like their parents, but not exactly the same.
Look again. The kittens have different spots and colours.
A mango seed is planted. What does it grow into?
Mango tree
Banana tree
Coconut tree
A mango seed grows into a mango tree.
Puppies from one family. Can they be different colours?
Yes, they can be different
No, never
Yes. Puppies look like their parents, but they can have different colours and spots.
Look at the puppies. Brothers and sisters can be different colours.
Why does a hen sit on her eggs?
To keep them warm
To break them
Because she is tired
Eggs need to stay warm so the chicks inside can grow.
Baby birds open their beaks and call. What does the parent do?
Brings them food
Flies away for good
Sings them to sleep
The parent brings them food until they can find their own.
Why does a mother cat carry her kitten in her mouth?
To move it somewhere safe
To play a game
To clean the floor
She moves it to a safe place. She holds the loose skin on its neck gently.
A baby cries. What do the parents do?
Find out what the baby needs
Leave the baby alone
Crying is how a baby says it is hungry, tired or hurting. Parents find out what it needs.
A baby cannot look after itself. Crying is how it asks for help.
Why do ducklings follow their mother?
To stay safe and learn
Because they are lost
To have a race
Staying close keeps them safe, and they learn how to find food.
A mother crocodile stays near her nest. Why?
To guard her eggs
To lay more eggs
To lie in the sun
She guards her eggs so other animals cannot eat them.
Put your hand on your throat and hum. What do you feel?
A buzzing shake
It gets hot
Nothing at all
A buzzing shake. Sound is made when something shakes fast. We call it a vibration.
You hit a drum. What does the top of the drum do?
It shakes
It melts
It stays still
The drum top shakes fast. The shaking makes the sound.
If it stayed still, there would be no sound. Sound comes from shaking.
A bell is ringing. You hold it tight. What happens?
The sound stops
It gets louder
Nothing changes
The sound stops, because the bell cannot shake any more.
Holding the bell stops it shaking. No shaking, no sound.
Put rice grains on a drum, then hit the drum. What do the grains do?
They jump
They grow
They melt
They jump! The shaking drum makes the rice move.
You hit the drum harder. How does it sound?
Louder
Quieter
The same
Louder. A bigger shake makes a louder sound.
A harder hit makes the drum shake more, so it is louder.
You pluck a guitar string. When does the sound stop?
When the string stops shaking
When you look away
It never stops
The sound stops when the string stops shaking.
The string slowly stops shaking, and then the sound stops.
Deep in a cave with no light at all. Can you see your hand?
No, we need light to see
Yes, if I look hard
No. We can only see things when there is light.
With no light at all, no one can see, even by looking hard.
Why does the Moon shine at night?
Sunlight shines on it
It makes its own light
It is a big lamp
The Sun shines on the Moon. The Moon does not make its own light.
The Moon is rock. It makes no light. It shines because the Sun lights it up.
The Moon is a ball of rock, not a lamp. The Sun lights it up.
What makes a shadow?
Something blocks the light
Water on the ground
The wind
Something blocks the light, so a dark shape forms behind it.
A shadow is not wet. It is where light cannot reach.
You shine a torch at a mirror. What does the light do?
It bounces back
It goes through
It disappears
It bounces back. Mirrors are smooth and shiny, so light bounces off them.
Light cannot pass through a mirror. It bounces off.
Your room is dark. How can you see your toys?
Turn on a light
Close my eyes
Be very quiet
Turn on a light. We need light to see.
Can a cat see when there is no light at all?
No, cats need some light too
Yes, perfectly
No. Cats see well in dim light, but with no light at all, no one can see.
Cats see well in dim light. But every eye needs some light to see.
Where does the Sun rise in the morning?
In the east
In the west
The Sun rises in the east every morning.
Where does the Sun set in the evening?
The Sun sets in the west every evening.
When is the Sun highest in the sky?
Around midday
Early morning
In the evening
Around midday, the Sun is at its highest.
Why can't we see stars in the daytime?
The Sun is too bright
The stars go away
The stars sleep
The stars are still there. The bright Sun hides them.
The stars are always there. The Sun's light is so bright we cannot see them.
Stars do not sleep. The Sun's light is so bright we cannot see them.
Can you sometimes see the Moon in the daytime?
Yes, sometimes
Yes. The Moon is often in the sky during the day too.
Look up on a clear day. You can often see a pale Moon.
When is your shadow shortest?
Late afternoon
Around midday. When the Sun is high, shadows are short. When it is low, they are long.
Does the Moon look the same shape every night?
No, its shape changes
Yes, it is always round
No. Its shape seems to change each night, and the pattern repeats about every month.
Watch for a few nights. The Moon goes from thin to round and back again.
In Cambodia, when is the rainy season?
About May to October
About December to February
There is none
Cambodia's rainy season is about May to October. The dry season is about November to April.
Which month is in Cambodia's dry season?
January
August
September
January is in the dry season. There is little rain.
When do Cambodian farmers plant most of their rice?
When the rains come
When the fields are dry and dusty
When the rains come. Rice needs lots of water to grow.
Rice needs lots of water, so most rice is planted when the rains come.
Dark clouds and thunder are coming. Where should you go?
Inside a building
Under a tall tree
Into the river
Go inside a building. That is the safest place in a storm.
Lightning often hits tall trees. Go inside a building.
Water is dangerous in a storm. Go inside a building.
In Cambodia, which month has longer days?
June
December
June. In Cambodia, June days are more than an hour longer than December days.
What helps you stay cool on a hot, dry day?
Shade and drinking water
A thick coat
Shade blocks the Sun, and drinking water cools your body.
Is it living or not living?
Living things eat or drink, grow, and have babies.
Living
Not living
Dog
Car
Tree
Ball
Rock
Book
Rice plant
Cup
A dog eats, grows and has puppies. It is living.
A car moves, but it does not eat, grow or have babies.
A tree drinks water, grows and makes seeds. It is living.
A ball can roll, but it does not grow or eat.
A fish eats, grows and lays eggs. It is living.
A toy robot moves, but it is not alive. It does not eat or grow.
A flower drinks water, grows and makes seeds. It is living.
A rock does not eat, drink or grow.
A snail eats leaves, grows and lays eggs. It is living.
A book does not eat, drink or grow.
A rice plant drinks water, grows and makes new rice grains. It is living.
A cup does not eat, drink or grow.
Does it make its own light?
Some things make light. Others only shine when light falls on them.
Makes light
No light of its own
Sun
Moon
Lamp
Mirror
Candle
Shiny spoon
Torch
Firefly
The Sun makes its own light. It lights up the whole day.
The Moon makes no light. It shines because the Sun lights it up.
A lamp makes light when it is switched on.
A mirror bounces light, but it makes none.
A candle flame makes light.
A shiny spoon bounces light. It does not make it.
A torch makes light when you switch it on.
A book makes no light. We see it when light shines on it.
A firefly makes its own light, to talk to other fireflies.
A rock makes no light. We see it when light shines on it.
Does light go through it?
Clear things let light through. Some things let a little through. Others block it.
See-through
Some light
Blocks light
Glass window
Thin paper
Wooden door
Glass of water
Thin cloth
Metal pot
Clear bottle
Cloudy plastic bag
Brick wall
Light goes straight through clear glass. You can see through it.
Thin paper lets some light through, but you cannot see clearly through it.
A wooden door blocks the light.
Clear water and glass let light through.
Thin cloth lets some light through, but not all.
A metal pot blocks the light.
A clear bottle lets light through.
A cloudy bag lets some light through, but you cannot see clearly.
A brick wall blocks all the light.
A book blocks the light.
Something is out of order. Tap a card to take it back.
How does a mango tree grow? Put it in order.
Sprout
Young tree
Tree with mangoes
A seed grows a sprout, then a young tree, then a big tree with fruit.
How does a chicken grow? Put it in order.
Egg
Chick
An egg hatches into a chick, and the chick grows into a hen.
How does a frog grow? Put it in order.
Eggs
Tadpole
Froglet
Eggs hatch into tadpoles. Tadpoles grow legs and become froglets, then frogs.
How does a butterfly grow? Put it in order.
Caterpillar
Chrysalis
An egg hatches into a caterpillar. It makes a chrysalis, and a butterfly comes out.
How does a person grow? Put it in order.
Baby
Grown-up
A baby grows into a child, and a child grows into a grown-up.
How does rice grow? Put it in order.
Young rice plants
Tall green rice
Golden rice
Harvest
Young rice plants grow tall and green, turn golden, then farmers harvest the grain.
Put the Sun's day in order.
Sunrise
Midday
Sunset
Night
The Sun rises, climbs high at midday, sets in the evening, and then it is night.
The Moon grows night by night. Put it in order.
Thin crescent
Half Moon
Full Moon
A thin crescent grows to a half Moon, then a full Moon.
Put the tree's shadow in order, from morning to evening.
Morning
Evening
Morning shadows are long. At midday they are short. In the evening they are long again, on the other side.
